title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer through a parenthesis must spell a Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge, not an argument position: the callee invokes a function it received inside an object literal, an array literal, a parenthesis, a cast or a `new` argument list exactly as it invokes one passed directly. Fail-closed matters here because the accepting behaviour is silent and wrong rather than loud and wrong — R1FIX executed this class before the fix and measured `isOk() === true` with a `Result` sitting in the SUCCESS payload, with zero language diagnostics and zero emitted-TypeScript diagnostics. A parenthesis changes nothing about the value that crosses the boundary, and the diagnostic is charged at the ARROW inside it rather than at the parenthesis — column 25, not column 24 — because the arrow is the function whose contract is missing. 07-must-consume/a-parenthesized-discard-is-charged-at-the-call pins the same one-column distinction for the must-consume rule.
